# Psalm 71 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** LORD, you are my shelter — don't ever let me be disgraced.

**2** Because you always do right, come to my rescue. Listen to my cry and save me!

**3** Be my safe place — the rock I can always run to. You've already decided to save me; you are my rock and my fortress.

**4** My God, pull me free from the grip of those who are cruel and merciless.

**5** You, Lord GOD, are everything I hope for — I've trusted you since I was young.

**6** I've depended on you from the day I was born — you brought me into this world. I will never stop praising you.

**7** Many people look at my life and are amazed, but you have been my strong protection through it all.

**8** All day long my mouth overflows with your praise and declares your splendor.

**9** Don't throw me aside when I'm old; don't abandon me when my strength gives out.

**10** My enemies talk about me behind my back; those plotting to kill me huddle together,

**11** saying, 'God has abandoned him. Go after him and grab him — no one will come to his rescue!'

**12** God, please don't stay far away! My God, hurry to help me!

**13** Let those who attack me be humiliated and destroyed; let those who want to harm me be buried in shame.

**14** But I will keep on hoping, and I will pile praise upon praise.

**15** I will tell everyone about how you make things right, about how you save — all day long, because there's more than I could ever count.

**16** I will come proclaiming the mighty things the Lord GOD has done; I will celebrate your justice — yours and no one else's.

**17** God, you've been teaching me since I was young, and I'm still telling people about the amazing things you do.

**18** Now that I'm old and gray, God, please don't leave me. Let me live to tell the next generation about your strength and power.

**19** Your justice, God, reaches to the heavens. You've done incredible things — God, there is no one like you!

**20** Even though you've let me go through terrible, crushing troubles, you will bring me back to life. You will pull me up from the deepest pit.

**21** You will make me greater than before and wrap me in comfort once again.

**22** Then I will praise your faithfulness on the harp, my God! I will make music to you on the lyre, Holy One of Israel!

**23** I will shout for joy as I sing your praises — because you have rescued my very soul.

**24** All day long I will talk about your justice, because those who tried to hurt me have been humiliated and put to shame.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **71:5-6**: This psalm has no superscription — unusual for Book II. The speaker looks back over an entire lifetime of trust, making it one of the most personal prayers in the Psalter.

- **71:9-11**: The fear of being discarded in old age is heartbreakingly human. Enemies exploit perceived divine abandonment — a theme that connects to Psalm 22.

- **71:20**: From the 'depths of the earth' — whether literal near-death or metaphorical despair, the promise of being brought back up is stunning in its confidence.

— PNEUMA
